verdict.rationale: pnpm documents per-project pinning of both tools and packages, and enforces those pins. Node.js can be pinned per project, and the `packageManager`/`devEngines.packageManager` field makes pnpm switch to the pinned pnpm version. Package versions are held by the lockfile with automatic frozen-lockfile mode in CI, plus catalogs and overrides for forcing versions. missing for 10: explicit docs on saving exact (non-range) specifiers in package.json, independent hands-on corroboration that tool/version pins are enforced.

support.subject: As a developer, I can pin exact versions of packages and tools per project and have the manager respect those pins

citations.quote: Install and pin Node.js per project straight from pnpm — no nvm, no shell hooks, no “works on my machine” version mismatches.
If your `package.json` has a `packageManager` or `devEngines.packageManager` field, pnpm switches to that version on first use
When pnpm detects that it is running in CI, it switches to frozen-lockfile mode automatically.
In a CI environment, installation fails if a lockfile is present but needs an update.
Define a dependency version once in pnpm-workspace.yaml and reference it as "catalog:" everywhere.
Add overrides to the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` file in order to force non-vulnerable versions of the dependencies.
